text:
alex: Quick heads-up — we've been seeing a sustained context length increase in APAC for the last 72h. Streaming sessions up ~35%, avg tokens/session up ~22% overall. This pushes GPU-hours forecast for next 30 days +18% vs baseline. Need to discuss capacity hedge.

meera: can you share the raw numbers+regions? is it model-specific?

alex: short breakdown — main spike on chat-v1 (t5-ish) and chat-legacy. Regions: ap-northeast1, ap-southeast1. quick table:

```
Region          | prev_tok/session | now_tok/session | streaming %
ap-northeast1   | 900              | 1700            | 68
ap-southeast1   | 1100             | 2400            | 58
us-west1        | 600              | 650             | 22
```

jon: that doubling in tok/session for ap-southeast1 is brutal. rough math: throughput drop ~40% for streaming mixes -> GPU-hr demand +~20%. do we need immediate capacity or can autoscaler catch up?

alex: autoscaler lagging because cooldowns and node provisioning times in those regions are 12–18m. For streaming, cold starts matter more. I recommend short-term buffer (reserved warm pool) + prewarm before peak windows.

sam: cost question — what's the commit delta? if we add a 15% buffer to APAC, how many GPU-hrs/week are we talking?

alex: ballpark: APAC baseline ~3500 GPU-hrs/week. +15% => ~525 GPU-hrs/week extra. If we buy dedicated reserved capacity it's cheaper, but commit vs spot calculus needed. I'll run Optimize sim.

oncall-bot: network: ALERT packet-loss spike 6% between ap-northeast1 <-> backbone (2026-02-14T08:12Z). Retries increased, could amplify token consumption.

meera: ugh network could explain retries + longer tail tokens. Mitigations: enable prefix/KV caching for chat-v1, increase client-side backoff, enable small-quant model fallback for streaming heavy clients.

alex: plan:
1) open infra ticket to add 15% warm buffer in ap-* (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4321)
2) tweak autoscaler: reduce cooldown and prefer node prewarm for streaming routes
3) add model routing policy to prefer quantized small-quant fallback when latency budget tight
4) run cost sim in Optimize and report by EOD tomorrow

jon: +1. Also can we throttle non-interactive long-context jobs to off-peak? maybe shift offline batches to night windows.

meera: agreed. I'll draft routing+policy PR. tagging @sam for cost review. :eyes:

sam: on it. I'll model reserved vs burst pricing and post numbers later today.

alex: thanks all. keeping watch on metrics, will ping if further spike. :thumbsup:
